proof.text: Put P = R[X_1,...,X_n], J = (f), C = P/J, F = kappa(p) tensor_R C, and K = kappa(q). The quotient map P -> C is surjective with kernel J. Mathlib Algebra.FormallySmooth.iff_split_injection gives a left inverse to the conormal map. KaehlerDifferential.exact_kerCotangentToTensor_mapBaseChange and Function.Exact.split_tfae' give C tensor_P Omega(P/R) isomorphic to J/J^2 times Omega(C/R). Extend its scalars from P to C using the surjective quotient map. The polynomial differential basis identifies the middle term with C^n.

Base change the preceding C-linear equivalence to K and distribute tensor product over the product with TensorProduct.prodRight. Base changing the given conormal basis and the coordinate basis gives ranks c and n. The differential module is finite because C is smooth, hence of finite type, over R. Module.finrank_prod and LinearEquiv.finrank_eq therefore give c + finrank_K(K tensor_C Omega(C/R)) = n.

KaehlerDifferential.tensorKaehlerEquiv identifies F tensor_C Omega(C/R) with Omega(F/kappa(p)). Base change this equivalence to K and use TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange to identify K tensor_C Omega(C/R) with K tensor_F Omega(F/kappa(p)). LinearEquiv.finrank_eq and natural-number arithmetic give the required rank n - c.

theorem smooth_quotient_fibre_finrank_eq_sub
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {n c : ℕ} (f : Fin c → MvPolynomial (Fin n) R)
    [Smooth R (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f))]
    (b : Module.Basis (Fin c)
      (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f))
      (Ideal.span (Set.range f)).Cotangent)
    (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime]
    (q : PrimeSpectrum (p.Fiber (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f)))) :
    Module.finrank q.asIdeal.ResidueField
      (q.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[p.Fiber
        (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f))]
          KaehlerDifferential p.ResidueField
            (p.Fiber (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f)))) = n - c
